Sean Gallagher: Heads up: perf-lab is getting noisy again. Seeing 10–25% swing run-to-run on the same config (H100) that we can’t explain w/ runtime changes. Looks like node contention / background jobs. Anyone else seeing this today?

Rina Kobayashi: yup. same matrix cell rerun 3x:
- run A: tok/s 182, p95 TPOT 58ms
- run B: tok/s 165, p95 TPOT 71ms
- run C: tok/s 179, p95 TPOT 60ms
Same container digest + pinned runtime commit.

Marcus Reed: I saw queue_wait spikes in the trace around prefill. Not just variance, it looks like the process is getting descheduled. CPU steal? Also noticed `nvidia-smi` reported fluctuating graphics clocks mid-run (not locked).

Allison Grant: I pulled node metrics for 2 of the “bad” runs. Both nodes had elevated disk IO + network TX during the benchmark window. Also saw bursts from `falcon-agent` and `log-collector` pods (daemonset) doing backfills.

Sean Gallagher: That matches what I suspected: we’re not truly “exclusive” on these nodes even when the benchmark pod is the only GPU consumer.

Sahana Iyer: CI/canary runs were also flaky last night. perf-canary flagged a regression then cleared on rerun. If lab isn’t stable, gating is going to be a mess.

Lena Fischer: what else is scheduled on those nodes? kube-system stuff + security agents? any cronjobs? also any GPU health checks?

Sean Gallagher: Current setup:
- K8s node pool `perf-lab-gpu` shared between bench + some ad-hoc profiling
- daemonsets: dcgm-exporter, node-exporter, fluent-bit, log-collector, falcon-agent
- there’s also a periodic “image pre-pull” job + a “gpu-burn” healthcheck job that was added a few weeks ago
I think those last two are the main offenders.

Hiro Tanaka: +1. We saw a similar issue in kernel microbench: background `gpu-burn` starts and you get weird transient throttling. Also the pre-pull can saturate disk and blow up latency.

Rina Kobayashi: Any chance we can get an actual dedicated slice? Like “no cron, no random jobs” nodes for benchmark harness.

Sean Gallagher: That’s the direction. Proposal:
1) Create a separate node pool `perf-lab-exclusive` (H100/H200/L40S) with:
   - taint `perf-exclusive=true:NoSchedule`
   - only benchmark pods tolerate it
   - deny ad-hoc pods by default
2) Disable/relocate the “image pre-pull” and “gpu-burn” jobs away from exclusive pool.
3) Priority classes: benchmark pods `system-cluster-critical` is too much, but we can set a high priority and set daemonsets to low priority (best-effort). Today, some daemons are bursty and preempt CPU.
4) Lock GPU clocks during runs (or at least record them). For NVIDIA: set application clocks or `nvidia-smi -lgc` inside privileged init (or a node-level setup script).

Allison Grant: + add “node cleanliness” tags into the artifacts so we can correlate. At minimum: node name, loadavg, disk read/write, net tx/rx, GPU power, graphics clock, SM clock, throttling reasons.

Marcus Reed: We already stamp node name + GPU UUID. Can extend the harness preflight to capture:
```
cat /proc/loadavg
cat /proc/pressure/cpu
iostat -xm 1 3
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=clocks.gr,clocks.sm,power.draw,temperature.gpu,clocks_throttle_reasons.active --format=csv
```
Then embed into the run metadata.

Sahana Iyer: If we’re locking clocks, can we do it without needing privileged pods? CI doesn’t love privileged. Could be a node bootstrap config instead.

Sean Gallagher: Agree. Better as node bootstrap. We can do:
- set persistence mode on
- set power limit
- set fixed clocks (where allowed)
But we need to be careful across SKUs (H100 vs L40S). Also some cloud images reset clocks on driver reload.

Lena Fischer: Also consider CPU isolation. If the benchmark process is sharing cores with log collectors, we’re going to see tail jitter. Any way to run benchmark pods with guaranteed CPU (no overcommit) + CPU manager static?

Sean Gallagher: Yes. For exclusive pool we can:
- kubelet `--cpu-manager-policy=static`
- benchmark pods request full cores, use `Guaranteed` QoS
- set `topologyManagerPolicy=best-effort` (or `restricted` if we want) to reduce NUMA weirdness
- disable CPU throttling surprises by making sure limits == requests

Allison Grant: Quick data point: the “bad” runs coincide with `log-collector` doing a 2–3 min backlog flush. It’s not GPU, but it hammers CPU + disk.

Rina Kobayashi: Can we just turn off log collection on perf nodes? We don’t need full logs there, just enough for infra health.

Sean Gallagher: I can reduce it. Maybe:
- keep node-exporter + dcgm-exporter
- reduce fluent-bit verbosity + lower resource requests
- disable heavy collectors on exclusive pool via nodeSelector

perf-lab-bot: (system) Node event: `gpu-burn` job started on node ip-10-84-13-22 at 2024-10-29T18:49:03Z (namespace: perf-tools)

Marcus Reed: lol there it is.

Hiro Tanaka: :facepalm: can we stop that today? we’re trying to measure FP8 prefill regressions and this is totally masking it.

Sean Gallagher: I’m going to disable `gpu-burn` in perf-tools for now (or at least remove it from `perf-lab-gpu`). Might need an approval from secops but we can scope it.

Sahana Iyer: For gating, can we add a “lab unstable” allowlist? Like if node cleanliness checks fail, mark run as invalid and don’t page people.

Allison Grant: That’s reasonable. We can define a couple of sanity thresholds:
- loadavg < X
- disk util < Y
- no throttle reasons active
If violated, tag run `invalid_env=true` and exclude from comparator.

Rina Kobayashi: +1. We can implement as a harness preflight and fail fast before spending 40 min on a matrix cell.

Sean Gallagher: Action items:
- [Sean] Hotfix today: stop `gpu-burn` / move it off perf nodes; also pause image pre-pull during benchmark windows.
- [Sean] Draft infra plan for `perf-lab-exclusive` node pool (taints/tolerations, daemonset selectors, cpu manager static). Will file internal ticket.
- [Allison] Provide list of metrics we should stamp + suggested thresholds for “invalid env”.
- [Rina/Marcus] Add preflight capture + env tagging to harness.
- [Sahana] Update canary job to ignore invalid runs + rerun on clean node.

Lena Fischer: For scheduling, should we implement a “reservation” system so two people don’t run matrices that collide? Even with exclusive pool, we could still contend if multiple benches launch.

Sean Gallagher: Yeah. Short-term we can cap concurrency via a namespace quota + limit range. Longer term: a simple “node lease” (configmap lock) per run so harness schedules one run per node.

Marcus Reed: If we add a lease, we should also ensure the harness requests 100% of GPU + enough CPU so K8s won’t co-locate accidentally.

Allison Grant: I’ll also add a dashboard panel: perf-lab node IO + daemon CPU over time, so we can see when the lab is “dirty”.

Sean Gallagher: Filed internal ticket for dedicated capacity + isolation changes (INT-842). Will link once it’s in.

Hiro Tanaka: Thanks. Please ping #eng-runtime when `gpu-burn` is off so we can rerun baselines.

Sean Gallagher: Will do. Disabling now and draining any nodes currently running it.

perf-lab-bot: (system) Change applied: CronJob `gpu-burn-nightly` suspended in namespace `perf-tools` by @sean.g (request id: PL-2281)

Rina Kobayashi: :thumbsup: rerunning the noisy cell now. Will report back.

Sahana Iyer: Once we have exclusive pool, can we also pin driver/CUDA versions per pool? We’ve been bitten by “helpful” image updates too.

Sean Gallagher: Yes. Exclusive pool will have pinned AMI + driver version, and we’ll roll it manually. Also we’ll block auto-upgrades during benchmark weeks.

Allison Grant: Dropping thresholds proposal here (rough):
- loadavg (1m) < 2.0 per CPU socket
- iostat util < 60% average during preflight
- `clocks_throttle_reasons.active` == 0
- dcgm “Xid errors in last 1h” == 0
We can refine after a couple days.

Sean Gallagher: Great. Let’s iterate but this is a good start. Once the rerun comes back we’ll see if variance tightens.

Rina Kobayashi: update: rerun on clean node: tok/s 181, p95 TPOT 59ms. basically matches “good” runs. so yeah, it was infra noise.

Sean Gallagher: Perfect confirmation. I’ll push the isolation work forward as priority for the sprint.
